Listen to this article Share Yam and plantain are familiar ingredients in Nigerian kitchens, but in Rivers State, they come together in a dish with a character of its own. Onunu is made by boiling yam and ripe plantain, then pounding them together with palm oil. It is enjoyed in Rivers State and among communities such as the Ijaw and Kalabari. The ripe plantain gives Onunu a gentle sweetness, while the yam provides its body. Palm oil brings the ingredients together and gives the dish its distinctive colour. Onunu is commonly served with fresh fish stew or catfish pepper soup, which complements its mild sweetness. Ingredients 1 medium tuber (peeled and cut into chunks or cubes) 2 -3 ripe plantains 1–2 tablespoons red palm oil Salt to taste Method Peel the yam, cut it into chunks and rinse thoroughly. Place the pieces in a pot, cover with water and bring to a boil. When the yam is partly cooked, add the ripe plantains. Some cooks boil the plantain with its skin on and peel it after cooking. Continue cooking until both the yam and plantain are soft. Remove the pot from the heat and drain the water. Peel the cooked plantain if it was boiled with the skin on. Transfer the yam to a clean mortar and pound until it begins to form a smooth, stretchy mass. Add the cooked plantain and continue pounding until it is evenly incorporated into the yam. Add the palm oil and salt a little at a time. Continue pounding until the mixture is smooth and the oil is fully combined. Shape the Onunu and serve warm with fresh fish stew or catfish pepper soup.
